on. See [#292](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/292).

## Inline Edge Styling

Use `linkStyle` to override edge colors and stroke widths — just like [Mermaid's linkStyle](https://mermaid.js.org/syntax/flowchart.html#styling-links):

```
graph TD
  A --> B --> C
  linkStyle 0 stroke:#ff0000,stroke-width:2px
  linkStyle default stroke:#888888
```

| Syntax                          | Effect                                 |
| ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `linkStyle 0 stroke:#f00`       | Style a single edge by index (0-based) |
| `linkStyle 0,2 stroke:#f00`     | Style multiple edges at once           |
| `linkStyle default stroke:#888` | Default style applied to all edges     |

Index-specific styles override the default. Supported properties: `stroke`, `stroke-width`.

Works in both flowcharts and state diagrams.

## XY Charts

Bar charts, line charts, and combinations — using Mermaid's `xychart-beta` syntax.

**Bar chart:**

```
xychart-beta
    title "Monthly Revenue"
    x-axis [Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, May, Jun]
    y-axis "Revenue ($K)" 0 --> 500
    bar [180, 250, 310, 280, 350, 420]
```

**Line chart:**

```
xychart-beta
    title "User Growth"
    x-axis [Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, May, Jun]
    line [1200, 1800, 2500, 3100, 3800, 4500]
```

**Combined bar + line:**

```
xychart-beta
    title "Sales with Trend"
    x-axis [Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, May, Jun]
    bar [300, 380, 280, 450, 350, 520]
    line [300, 330, 320, 353, 352, 395]
```

**Horizontal orientation:**

```
xychart-beta horizontal
    title "Language Popularity"
    x-axis [Python, JavaScript, Java, Go, Rust]
    bar [30, 25, 20, 12, 8]
```

**Axis configuration:**

- Categorical x-axis: `x-axis [A, B, C]`
- Numeric x-axis range: `x-axis 0 --> 100`
- Axis titles: `x-axis "Category" [A, B, C]`
- Y-axis range: `y-axis "Score" 0 --> 100`

**Multi-series:** Add multiple `bar` and/or `line` declarations. Each series gets a distinct color from a monochromatic palette derived from the theme's accent color.

For the original design proposal behind this feature, see [xychart-design.md](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/blob/main/docs/xychart-design.md) (historical).

### XY Chart Styling

The chart renderer follows a clean, minimal design philosophy, originally inspired by Apple's design language and Craft's interface for `beautiful-mermaid`:

- **Dot grid** — A subtle dot pattern fills the plot area instead of traditional solid grid lines
- **Rounded bars** — All bar corners are rounded for a modern, polished look
- **Smooth curves** — Line series use natural cubic spline interpolation, producing mathematically smooth curves through all data points (not straight segments or staircase steps)
- **Floating labels** — No visible axis lines or tick marks; labels float freely for a clutter-free aesthetic
- **Drop-shadow lines** — Each line series has a subtle shadow beneath it for depth
- **Monochromatic palette** — Series 0 uses the theme's accent color; additional series get darker/lighter shades of the same hue with subtle hue drift, adapting automatically to light or dark backgrounds
- **Interactive tooltips** — When rendered with `interactivity: 'full'` (or the deprecated `interactive: true`), hovering over bars or data points shows value tooltips. Multi-line tooltips appear when multiple series share an x-position
- **Sparse line dots** — Lines with 12 or fewer data points show data point dots by default for readability
- **Full theme support** — All 15 built-in themes (and custom themes) apply to charts. The accent color drives the entire series color palette
- **Live theme switching** — Chart series colors are CSS custom properties (`--xychart-color-N`), so theme changes apply instantly without re-rendering

## Architecture Diagrams

`architecture-beta` (and the bare `architecture` header) follows
[Mermaid's syntax](https://mermaid.ai/open-source/syntax/architecture.html):

```mermaid
architecture-beta
  group api(cloud)[API]
  service db(database)[Database] in api
  service server(server)[Server] in api
  service client(internet)[Client]
  db:L -- R:server
  server:T <--> B:client
```

Supported: `group`, `service` and `junction` (with `in <group>` nesting and
optional `(icon)` / `[Title]`), edges with port sides and `--`, `-->`, `<--`,
`<-->`, and the `{group}` modifier (the edge attaches to the service's
enclosing group). A statement the parser does not understand is an error with
its line number, not silently dropped.

The diagram is lowered to the flowchart model and drawn by the flowchart
layout, so it is not positioned on Mermaid's port grid:

- Ports only choose the flow direction (left-to-right unless more edges use
  top/bottom ports) and which way each edge points in the layout, so
  `db:L -- R:server` still puts `server` left of `db`. Exact placement is the
  flowchart layout's.
- Icons are not drawn. `database` and `disk` give a cylinder, `cloud` a
  stadium, `internet` a circle; any other icon (including custom `"pack:name"`
  icons) gives a rectangle.
- `align row` / `align column` are accepted and ignored.
- ASCII draws a junction as an empty box and, like any flowchart, can mis-place
  nodes when sibling groups are joined by cross-group edges.

## C4 Diagrams

`C4Context`, `C4Container`, `C4Component`, `C4Dynamic` and `C4Deployment` diagrams render in both SVG and ASCII.

```
C4Container
  Person(user, "User")
  System_Boundary(shop, "Shop") {
    Container(web, "Web App", "React", "Storefront")
    ContainerDb(db, "Database", "PostgreSQL")
  }
  Rel(user, web, "Browses")
  Rel(web, db, "Reads/writes", "SQL")
```

Supported: `Person`, `System`, `Container`, `Component` (plus `Db`, `Queue` and `_Ext` variants), `Boundary`/`Enterprise_Boundary`/`System_Boundary`/`Container_Boundary`, `Deployment_Node`/`Node`/`Node_L`/`Node_R`, `Rel`, `BiRel`, directional `Rel_*` aliases, `RelIndex`, and `title`.

C4 diagrams have their own renderers (they are not lowered to the flowchart model): persons get a head-and-shoulders glyph, databases a cylinder, queues a pipe, external elements the muted C4 palette, and boundaries and deployment nodes a dashed frame with a title. Relationship labels show the label and, on its own line, the `[technology]`. A `title` is drawn at the top. `Rel` endpoints may be populated boundaries. `RenderOptions.direction` re-orients the SVG layout (default top-to-bottom).

Layout hints: `Rel_D`/`Rel_U`/`Rel_L`/`Rel_R` are layering constraints (target below/above, or side by side in one row) in ASCII. In SVG they have no effect on placement, as in Mermaid: shapes are laid out in declaration order, in rows, and relationships are drawn afterwards without moving anything. C4 SVG uses its own row layout, not ELK, so it does not need `elkjs`.

Known limitations:

- ASCII output is always top-to-bottom (`BT` reverses the rows; `LR`/`RL` are laid out top-to-bottom).
- `UpdateElementStyle`, `UpdateRelStyle`, `UpdateLayoutConfig`, legends and tags are accepted and ignored. Elements use the standard C4 palette.
- A relationship from an element to itself is not drawn in ASCII.
- Two relationships with the same `from` and `to` (for example `Rel(a, b, ...)` and `Rel_Back(a, b, ...)`) are both drawn. Mermaid merges them and draws only the later one; we keep both so nothing the author wrote is dropped (#1209).

## Pie Charts

`pie` follows [Mermaid's syntax](https://mermaid.ai/open-source/syntax/pie.html)
and its renderer's layout:

```mermaid
pie showData title Key elements in Product X
  "Calcium" : 42.96
  "Potassium" : 50.05
  "Magnesium" : 10.01
  "Iron" : 5
```

Supported: `title` (on the `pie` line or its own line), `showData` (right
after `pie`), quoted `"label" : value` slices, `accTitle` and `accDescr`.
Values must be zero or more; a repeated label keeps its first value. A line
the parser does not understand is an error with its line number.

The SVG uses Mermaid's geometry: slices in source order, clockwise from 12
o'clock; each slice labelled with its whole-number percentage of the total,
inside the slice; a legend on the right listing every slice (with `showData`,
as `label [value]`, the value printed as written). Slices under 1% of the
total are left out of the pie but stay in the legend, so the drawn slices
fill the circle and the labels may not add up to 100%. A `pie` with no
slices draws an empty circle.

Colours follow the theme instead of Mermaid's `pie1`..`pie12` (unless you opt
in with `honorThemeVariables`, see [`themeVariables`](#themevariables-opt-in)):
the first slice uses the accent colour, the next eleven use the XY chart series
shades, and the twelve repeat after that. Slices are drawn at Mermaid's 0.7
opacity with a 2px outline in the theme's foreground colour.

Known differences from Mermaid:

- `%%{init: {"pie": {"textPosition": 0.5}}}%%` moves the SVG slice labels
  (0 is the centre, 1 the outer edge; default 0.75). The ASCII output has no
  positioned labels, so it ignores it.
- `%%{init: {"pie": {"donutHole": 0.5}}}%%` cuts a hole in the SVG pie, as a
  fraction of the radius. Like Mermaid, it only applies for values above 0
  and up to 0.9 (anything else draws a plain pie), and the slice labels stay
  at `textPosition`. The ASCII output has no centre to cut, so it ignores it.
- `%%{init: {"pie": {"legendPosition": "left"}}}%%` moves the SVG legend
  (`right` is the default, then `left`, `top`, `bottom` or `center`; anything
  else draws the default). `left` and `top` shift the pie to make room, `top`
  and `bottom` make the frame taller, and `center` draws the legend over the
  pie. As in Mermaid, the title stays centred on the frame, not on a shifted
  pie. The ASCII output always puts the legend beside the bars, so it ignores
  it.
- `%%{init: {"pie": {"highlightSlice": "Cats"}}}%%` draws the slice with that
  exact label 5% larger and fully opaque, as Mermaid 12.1.0 does (it scales the
  slice about the pie centre; it does not pull it out). `"hover"` only
  applies under a pointer, so a static image ignores it, and so does the ASCII
  output. See
  [the decision](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/blob/main/docs/decisions/pie-highlight-slice-static-1726.md).
- A legend taller than the 450px frame (more than about 20 slices), or a
  `top`/`bottom`/`center` legend wider than it, makes the SVG larger instead of
  being cut off, and an empty chart keeps its full
  width (Mermaid crops it).
- Mermaid's `#quot;`-style character codes in pie labels and legends are shown as written. Flowchart labels decode them (via `decodeMermaidEntities` in `packages/core/src/multiline-utils.ts`).

Mermaid has no text output for pie charts; see
[ASCII Pie Charts](#ascii-pie-charts) for this library's.

## Quadrant Charts

`quadrantChart` follows [Mermaid's syntax](https://mermaid.ai/open-source/syntax/quadrantChart.html)
and its renderer's layout, checked against `mermaid@12.2.0` (the pin, which is
also npm `latest`):

```mermaid
quadrantChart
    title Reach and engagement of campaigns
    x-axis Low Reach --> High Reach
    y-axis Low Engagement --> High Engagement
    quadrant-1 We should expand
    quadrant-2 Need to promote
    quadrant-3 Re-evaluate
    quadrant-4 May be improved
    Campaign A: [0.3, 0.6]
    Campaign B: [0.45, 0.23]
```

Supported: `title`, `x-axis` and `y-axis` (one label or `left --> right`),
`quadrant-1` to `quadrant-4` (1 is top right, then counter-clockwise), points as
`label: [x, y]` with `x` and `y` between 0 and 1, `classDef` with
`:::class` on a point, the four point styles (`radius`, `color`,
`stroke-color`, `stroke-width`, validated with Mermaid's messages), `accTitle`
and `accDescr`. As in Mermaid, coordinates must be `0`, `1` or `0.<digits>`
(`1.5`, `-0.2` and `.5` are errors), a trailing `-->` keeps its arrow in the
label (`Effort ⟶`), and a bare `quadrantChart` is valid.

The SVG uses Mermaid's geometry: a 500 x 500 frame, four equal cells, the x
axis above the plot until the chart has a point and below it after, quadrant
labels centred while there are no points and on the cells' top row once there
are, and the last point in the source drawn first. Colours come from the theme
(the accent mixed into `--bg` at four falling strengths for the cells), so
every theme and live theme switching apply. Text is not measured; a label wider
than its cell overflows, as in Mermaid. Not read yet: `quadrantChart` config in
`%%{init}%%` (`chartWidth`, `pointRadius`, ...), the quadrant `themeVariables`,
and `%%{init}%%` / front matter themes for this type. See
[Known differences](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/blob/main/docs/known-differences.md#quadrant-charts).

### ASCII Quadrant Charts

Mermaid has no text mode for quadrant charts, so the ASCII output is this
library's own design: the same four cells on a character grid.

```text
                 Reach and engagement of campaigns

                ┌────────────────────────┬────────────────────────┐
                │    Need to promote     │    We should expand    │
                │                        │                        │
                │                        │                        │
High Engagement │                 6      │                        │
                │                        │  3                     │
                │                        │                        │
                │              1         │                        │
                ├────────────────────────┼────────────────────────┤
                │      Re-evaluate       │    May be improved     │
                │                   5    │            4           │
                │                        │                        │
 Low Engagement │                      2 │                        │
                │                        │                        │
                │                        │                        │
                │                        │                        │
                └────────────────────────┴────────────────────────┘
                        Low Reach                High Reach

  1 Campaign A  (0.3, 0.6)
  2 Campaign B  (0.45, 0.23)
```

- **Cells** are at least 24 columns wide (wider for a longer quadrant label,
  measured in terminal columns) and 7 rows tall.
- **Points** are one marker character (`1`-`9`, `A`-`Z`, `a`-`z`, then `*`)
  at the cell their coordinates fall on; labels would collide, so a legend
  below lists marker, label and the coordinates as written. A marker that
  would land on a quadrant label or another marker moves to the nearest free
  cell, preferring downwards. A point's own `color` paints its marker; the
  others use the theme accent.
- **Axes:** a trailing arrow (`Effort ⟶` in the SVG) is `→`, or `->` in ASCII mode; the y labels sit in a left gutter on the middle row of each half
  (the bottom row for a one-sided axis); the x labels sit under the halves,
  always below the grid, unlike the SVG's x axis on top of a point-free chart.
- `accTitle` and `accDescr` are not printed.

## Unsupported upstream diagram types

These Mermaid diagram types are not rendered; `renderMermaidSVG` and the CLI reject them with "Invalid mermaid header". Checked against `mermaid@12.2.0` (npm `latest`, 2026-10-13) by parsing each header with `mermaid.parse`. Use case diagrams (added in Mermaid 12.0.0) are out of scope for now: upstream still gates them behind `usecase-beta` (plain `usecase` is not detected) and there is no demand here yet. Support is tracked in [#2085](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/2085).

| Type                                                                  | Header                                                                                                          |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Use case                                                              | `usecase-beta`                                                                                                  |
| Mindmap                                                               | `mindmap`                                                                                                       |
| Packet                                                                | `packet` / `packet-beta`                                                                                        |
| Gantt                                                                 | `gantt`                                                                                                         |
| Timeline                                                              | `timeline`                                                                                                      |
| User journey                                                          | `journey`                                                                                                       |
| Requirement                                                           | `requirementDiagram`                                                                                            |
| Git graph                                                             | `gitGraph`                                                                                                      |
| Kanban                                                                | `kanban`                                                                                                        |
| Radar                                                                 | `radar-beta`                                                                                                    |
| Treemap                                                               | `treemap-beta`                                                                                                  |
| Tree view, Venn, Wardley, Ishikawa, Cynefin, Railroad, Event modeling | `treeView-beta`, `venn-beta`, `wardley-beta`, `ishikawa-beta`, `cynefin-beta`, `railroad-beta`, `eventmodeling` |
| Sankey, Block                                                         | `sankey-beta`, `block-beta` (12.2.0 rejects them with an empty body; header names per upstream docs)            |

## Accessibility

Every SVG diagram type gets `role="img"` on the root `<svg>`, so assistive
tech treats it as one image instead of a group whose node/edge labels get
announced individually and out of reading order.

```ts
renderMermaidSVG('graph TD\n  A --> B', {
  title: 'Flowchart: Build → Test → Ship',
})
```

`title` supplies the accessible name: `aria-labelledby` on the root points
at a `<title id="zm-title-N">` child holding the text — the standard
SVG/WAI-ARIA technique for naming inline SVG. The `zm-title-N` id is unique
per render call, so multiple diagrams inlined into one page never collide.
This library never invents a name on your behalf (a generated "flowchart
with 3 nodes" summary would be a confidently useless accessible name) — when
`title` is omitted the SVG still gets `role="img"`, but claims no name, the
same as an `<img>` with no `alt`.

Every diagram type reads Mermaid's `accTitle:` and `accDescr:` statements
([Mermaid docs](https://mermaid.js.org/config/accessibility.html)): put
`accTitle: text` and `accDescr: text` on one line, or `accDescr { ... }` over
several lines, anywhere after the header. `accTitle` becomes the accessible
name when the `title` option is not given (the option wins; for C4 the order is
option, `accTitle`, then the C4 `title`), and `accDescr` becomes a
`<desc id="zm-desc-N">` referenced by `aria-describedby`. The statements are
never drawn, and both are dropped when the diagram is `decorative`. ASCII output
ignores them. The visible chart `title` of a pie chart is not used as its
accessible name.

For a diagram that's already described in surrounding prose, mark it
decorative instead of naming it:

```ts
renderMermaidSVG('graph TD\n  A --> B', { decorative: true })
```

This emits `aria-hidden="true"` in place of `role`/`aria-labelledby`/`<title>`,
and `title`, if also given, is ignored.

This is independent of the per-node/per-point `<title>` tooltips from
[Interactions](#interactions) (`click A "url" "Tooltip"`) and the XY chart's
`interactive` hover tips — those are unid'd `<title>` elements nested inside
each node/point's `<g>`, so they never collide with the root's generated id.

**A `click A "url"` link overrides both `role="img"` and `decorative`.** A
link renders as a real, focusable `<a href>` nested inside the SVG. Both
`role="img"` (which tells assistive tech to stop descending into children)
and `aria-hidden="true"` (which must never contain a focusable descendant,
per the WAI-ARIA spec) would make that link Tab-reachable but invisible to a
screen reader — so when any node has a link, the root gets no `role` at all,
regardless of what `title`/`decorative` asked for. `title` still applies if
given. See [issue #239](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/239).

## ASCII Rendering

For terminal environments, CLI tools, or anywhere you need plain text, render to ASCII or Unicode box-drawing characters:

```typescript
import { renderMermaidASCII } from 'zombie-mermaid'

// Unicode mode (default) — prettier box drawing
const unicode = renderMermaidASCII(`graph LR; A --> B`)

// Pure ASCII mode — maximum compatibility
const ascii = renderMermaidASCII(`graph LR; A --> B`, { useAscii: true })
```

If you only need ASCII output, import from `zombie-mermaid/ascii` instead —
it never loads the SVG renderer or `elkjs`, the SVG layout engine (an optional
peer you register with `registerElk()`):

```typescript
import { renderMermaidASCII } from 'zombie-mermaid/ascii'
```

**Unicode output:**

```
┌───┐     ┌───┐
│   │     │   │
│ A │────►│ B │
│   │     │   │
└───┘     └───┘
```

**ASCII output:**

```
+---+     +---+
|   |     |   |
| A |---->| B |
|   |     |   |
+---+     +---+
```

### ASCII Options

```typescript
renderMermaidASCII(diagram, {
  useAscii: false,      // true = ASCII, false = Unicode (default)
  paddingX: 5,          // Horizontal spacing between nodes
  paddingY: 5,          // Vertical spacing (default 5; in LR and RL the gap between sibling nodes is paddingY - 1, minimum 1)
  boxBorderPadding: 1,  // Padding inside node boxes
  colorMode: 'auto',    // 'none' | 'auto' | 'ansi16' | 'ansi256' | 'truecolor' | 'html'
  theme: { ... },       // Partial<AsciiTheme> — override default colors
  hyperlinks: false,    // true = OSC 8 terminal hyperlinks for `click` hrefs
})
```

### ASCII terminal hyperlinks

A `click A "https://..."` directive normally has nowhere to go in text
output. With `hyperlinks: true`, each node whose `click` declared an
http/https/mailto/relative href gets its label wrapped in an
[OSC 8](https://gist.github.com/egmontkob/eb114294efbcd5adb1944c9f3cb5feda)
escape pair (`ESC ] 8 ; ; <url> ESC \` … `ESC ] 8 ; ; ESC \`), which
terminals that support it — iTerm2, WezTerm, kitty, Windows Terminal,
VTE-based terminals such as GNOME Terminal — render as a clickable link. The
sequences are zero-width: they never change layout, box drawing, or column
widths, and stripping them yields exactly the non-hyperlinked output.
Flowchart nodes and class-diagram class names are linked; `click ... call
fn()` bindings emit nothing, and unsafe schemes (`javascript:`, `data:`) are
dropped by the same filter the SVG renderer uses.

It is off by default, and the library does no terminal capability
detection: not every terminal or pager handles OSC 8 gracefully (`less`
needs `-R` and a recent version), so the caller decides. The option is
ignored in `colorMode: 'html'`, which is rendered by a browser rather than a
terminal. From the CLI, pass `--hyperlinks` alongside `--ascii`.

**Known limitations.** macOS's built-in Terminal.app has never implemented
OSC 8 — it silently swallows the escape sequences rather than rendering a
link, so a hyperlinked label looks identical to a plain one and clicking it
does nothing (verified against Terminal.app on macOS 26). It is not on the
list above; if links aren't clickable, check which terminal is actually in
use before assuming the renderer is broken. IDE-integrated terminals (VS
Code, and others built on the same terminal component) do support OSC 8, but
only for `http`/`https` hrefs — a `mailto:` or relative link may render with
link styling there without actually being clickable. See
[egmontkob's terminal-hyperlink support matrix](https://gist.github.com/egmontkob/eb114294efbcd5adb1944c9f3cb5feda)
for the current state across emulators.

### ASCII XY Charts

XY charts render to ASCII with dedicated chart-drawing characters:

- **Bar charts** — `█` blocks (Unicode) or `#` (ASCII mode)
- **Line charts** — Staircase routing with rounded corners: `╭╮╰╯│─` (Unicode) or `+|-` (ASCII)
- **Multi-series** — Each series gets a distinct ANSI color from the theme's accent palette
- **Legends** — Automatically shown when multiple series are present
- **Horizontal charts** — Fully supported with categories on the y-axis
- **Y-axis ticks** — The same ticks as the SVG, and as Mermaid.js: about 10 intervals at a step of 1, 2 or 5 times a power of ten. Without a `y-axis` range the axis spans the data's own minimum and maximum, so bars start at the data minimum; see [xychart-design.md](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/blob/main/docs/xychart-design.md#shipped-behavior-y-axis-ticks-and-the-y-axis-title)
- **Y-axis title** — Written one letter per row down the left edge in vertical charts (no rotation in a terminal), and as a centered line under the axis in horizontal charts

### ASCII Pie Charts

Mermaid has no text mode for pie charts, so the ASCII output is this
library's own design: one stacked bar, 50 cells wide, and a table below it.
The numbers are the SVG renderer's.

```text
             Pets adopted by volunteers

[████████████████████████████████████████▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▒]

  █ Dogs    79%
  ▓ Cats    17%
  ▒ Rats     3%
```

- **The bar** holds the slices at or above 1% of the total, in source order,
  sharing all 50 cells between them, as the SVG's drawn slices share the
  circle. Cells are rounded by largest remainder, so the segments always add
  up to 50, and every drawn slice gets at least one cell (with more than 50
  slices at 1% or more, the ones that lose out on the rounding get none).
- **The table** is the SVG legend: one row per slice, in source order, with
  `label [value]` under `showData` (the value printed as written). The
  percentage is the SVG's slice label, a whole number of the full total.
  A slice with no segment (under 1%, or left without a cell) has no
  percentage, and a `·` (`.` in ASCII mode) as its swatch.
- **Fills** tell segments apart: `█▓▒░` (Unicode) or `#=*+` (ASCII),
  cycling so that neighbouring segments always differ; each table swatch
  repeats its segment's fill. This holds in every colour mode, because two
  neighbouring palette shades can land on the same terminal colour
  (especially in `ansi16`).
- **Colour** uses the SVG palette, painted over the fills: the accent, then
  the XY chart series shades, repeating after 12.
- The title is centred over the bar. `accTitle` and `accDescr` are not
  printed (in the SVG they are the accessible name and description, not
  visible text).
- Long labels are never truncated or wrapped; the table widens to fit them,
  measured in terminal columns so CJK and emoji labels line up.
- A chart with no slices prints an empty bar.

---

# https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/blob/main/docs/theming.md

# Theming

The theming system is the heart of `zombie-mermaid`: a small set of inputs drives every derived color in a diagram.

## The Two-Color Foundation

Every diagram needs just two colors: **background** (`bg`) and **foreground** (`fg`). That's it. From these two colors, the entire diagram is derived using `color-mix()`:

```typescript
const svg = renderMermaidSVG(diagram, {
  bg: '#1a1b26', // Background
  fg: '#a9b1d6', // Foreground
})
```

This is **Mono Mode**—a coherent, beautiful diagram from just two colors. The system automatically derives:

| Element        | Derivation                |
| -------------- | ------------------------- |
| Text           | `--fg` at 100%            |
| Secondary text | `--fg` at 60% into `--bg` |
| Edge labels    | `--fg` at 40% into `--bg` |
| Faint text     | `--fg` at 25% into `--bg` |
| Connectors     | `--fg` at 50% into `--bg` |
| Arrow heads    | `--fg` at 85% into `--bg` |
| Node fill      | `--fg` at 3% into `--bg`  |
| Group header   | `--fg` at 5% into `--bg`  |
| Inner strokes  | `--fg` at 12% into `--bg` |
| Node stroke    | `--fg` at 20% into `--bg` |

## Enriched Mode

For richer themes, you can provide optional "enrichment" colors that override specific derivations:

```typescript
const svg = renderMermaidSVG(diagram, {
  bg: '#1a1b26',
  fg: '#a9b1d6',
  // Optional enrichment:
  line: '#3d59a1', // Edge/connector color
  accent: '#7aa2f7', // Arrow heads, highlights
  muted: '#565f89', // Secondary text, labels
  surface: '#292e42', // Node fill tint
  border: '#3d59a1', // Node stroke
})
```

If an enrichment color isn't provided, it falls back to the `color-mix()` derivation. This means you can provide just the colors you care about.

## Pie, C4 and architecture diagrams

Pie charts read `--accent` live for the first slice and derive the other
slices from it and `--bg`; the outline and slice strokes use `--fg`. C4
element fills, strokes and text use fixed Mermaid palette colours, so they do
not follow the theme; boundaries, relationship lines, titles and labels use the
theme's foreground. Architecture
diagrams are rendered through the flowchart renderer, so they consume every
enrichment colour exactly as flowcharts do.

## CSS Custom Properties = Live Switching

All colors are CSS custom properties on the `<svg>` element. This means you can switch themes instantly without re-rendering:

```javascript
// Switch theme by updating CSS variables
svg.style.setProperty('--bg', '#282a36')
svg.style.setProperty('--fg', '#f8f8f2')
// The entire diagram updates immediately
```

For React apps, pass CSS variable references instead of hex values:

```typescript
const svg = renderMermaidSVG(diagram, {
  bg: 'var(--background)',
  fg: 'var(--foreground)',
  accent: 'var(--accent)',
  transparent: true,
})
// Theme switches apply automatically via CSS cascade — no re-render needed
```

## Resolved Colors for Rasterizers

Live switching works because browsers evaluate `var()` and `color-mix()`. Non-browser consumers — resvg, librsvg, Inkscape, ImageMagick, most PDF pipelines — don't, and render every derived color as black. For output headed to one of those, ask for the computed values instead:

```typescript
const svg = renderMermaidSVG(diagram, {
  ...THEMES['tokyo-night'],
  resolveColors: true,
})
// No var() or color-mix() left: every color is a concrete #rrggbb / rgba()
```

```bash
zombie-mermaid render diagram.mmd --svg -o out.svg --theme tokyo-night --resolve-colors
```

The substitution uses the same mix percentages the `<style>` block declares (the `MIX` table in `packages/core/src/theme.ts`), so it can't drift from what a browser would compute. The trade-off is that the output is now a fixed palette — setting `--bg`/`--fg` on it later does nothing — and a color you passed as a `var(--…)` reference can't be resolved (there's no host page to ask), so it's left untouched.

The CLI's `render --png` (see [README](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/blob/main/README.md#cli)) does this resolution automatically — there's no separate `--resolve-colors --png` step to remember, since a rasterizer needs it unconditionally.

## Built-in Themes

15 themes ship out of the box:

| Theme               | Type  | Background | Accent    |
| ------------------- | ----- | ---------- | --------- |
| `zinc-light`        | Light | `#FFFFFF`  | Derived   |
| `zinc-dark`         | Dark  | `#18181B`  | Derived   |
| `tokyo-night`       | Dark  | `#1a1b26`  | `#7aa2f7` |
| `tokyo-night-storm` | Dark  | `#24283b`  | `#7aa2f7` |
| `tokyo-night-light` | Light | `#d5d6db`  | `#34548a` |
| `catppuccin-mocha`  | Dark  | `#1e1e2e`  | `#cba6f7` |
| `catppuccin-latte`  | Light | `#eff1f5`  | `#8839ef` |
| `nord`              | Dark  | `#2e3440`  | `#88c0d0` |
| `nord-light`        | Light | `#eceff4`  | `#5e81ac` |
| `dracula`           | Dark  | `#282a36`  | `#bd93f9` |
| `github-light`      | Light | `#ffffff`  | `#0969da` |
| `github-dark`       | Dark  | `#0d1117`  | `#4493f8` |
| `solarized-light`   | Light | `#fdf6e3`  | `#268bd2` |
| `solarized-dark`    | Dark  | `#002b36`  | `#268bd2` |
| `one-dark`          | Dark  | `#282c34`  | `#c678dd` |

```typescript
import { renderMermaidSVG, THEMES } from 'zombie-mermaid'

const svg = renderMermaidSVG(diagram, THEMES['tokyo-night'])
```

## Adding Your Own Theme

At minimum, a theme just needs `bg` and `fg`:

```typescript
const myTheme = {
  bg: '#0f0f0f',
  fg: '#e0e0e0',
}

const svg = renderMermaidSVG(diagram, myTheme)
```

Want richer colors? Add any of the optional enrichments:

```typescript
const myRichTheme = {
  bg: '#0f0f0f',
  fg: '#e0e0e0',
  accent: '#ff6b6b', // Pop of color for arrows
  muted: '#666666', // Subdued labels
}
```

## Full Shiki Compatibility

Use **any VS Code theme** directly via Shiki integration. This gives you access to hundreds of community themes:

```typescript
import { getSingletonHighlighter } from 'shiki'
import { renderMermaidSVG, fromShikiTheme } from 'zombie-mermaid'

// Load any theme from Shiki's registry
const highlighter = await getSingletonHighlighter({
  themes: ['vitesse-dark', 'rose-pine', 'material-theme-darker'],
})

// Extract diagram colors from the theme
const colors = fromShikiTheme(highlighter.getTheme('vitesse-dark'))

const svg = renderMermaidSVG(diagram, colors)
```

The `fromShikiTheme()` function intelligently maps VS Code editor colors to diagram roles:

| Editor Color                  | Diagram Role |
| ----------------------------- | ------------ |
| `editor.background`           | `bg`         |
| `editor.foreground`           | `fg`         |
| `editorLineNumber.foreground` | `line`       |
| `focusBorder` / keyword token | `accent`     |
| comment token                 | `muted`      |
| `editor.selectionBackground`  | `surface`    |
| `editorWidget.border`         | `border`     |

---

# https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/blob/main/docs/known-differences.md

# Known differences from mermaid.js

Places where zombie-mermaid renders or parses differently from mermaid.js and the
difference is either intentional or not yet fixed. The reference is the pinned
`mermaid` devDependency (12.2.0), rendered headless through
`scripts/lib/real-mermaid.ts`; GitHub renders 12.1.0 and mermaid.live 12.2.0 (see the
table below). The pin matches mermaid.live, not GitHub.
The pin moved from 11.17.2 in the bump that added this note, and entries not
listed below as re-checked were measured on 11.17.2: other versions may differ.
The "Labeled Fan-In (LR)" mirrored-order entry that used to sit under layout
tie-breaks was removed after a re-check: on 12.1.0 mermaid and zombie-mermaid agree
(100% / 100%, it was 17% on 11.17.2).

## Which mermaid each surface renders (checked 2026-10-22, #2184)

| Surface                        | mermaid | Default layout | Evidence                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------ | ------- | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Pinned oracle (`package.json`) | 12.2.0  | ELK            | `mermaid.mermaidAPI.getConfig().layout` is `elk` headless                                                                  |
| GitHub ` ```mermaid ` blocks   | 12.1.0  | ELK (config)   | Renderer bundle `viewscreen.githubusercontent.com/static/assets/mermaidMarkdown-*.js` matches 12.1.0, not 12.0.0 or 12.2.0 |
| mermaid.live                   | 12.2.0  | ELK            | The editor shows `v12.2.0`; node positions equal the headless ELK render                                                   |

GitHub's bundle reports `version:"0.0.0"` and its renderer sits in a cross-origin
iframe, so its version is inferred, not read: it contains identifiers added in 12.1.0
(`orientFeedbackEdges`, `applyOverride`) and none of the 12.2.0 additions
(`upperCaseDirection`, `isUnconnected`, `colorBy`). 12.1.0 and 12.2.0 place the dense
samples identically (gallery "Dense Duplicate Edges" TD and LR, and the #2160 sample 3
with and without `n0["n0"]`/`n1["n1"]` declarations), so either version is a valid target on
both surfaces; `layout: dagre` places them differently. Re-run the check when the pin
moves; `tsx scripts/lib/mermaid-pin-freshness.ts` prints the last versions seen.

## Subgraph inner direction

Re-checked on 12.1.0 (and 11.17.2). Given `subgraph S` holding `a --> b --> c` in a
`graph TD`:

- **No `direction`.** mermaid 11.17.2 flipped an uncrossed subgraph perpendicular to
  its parent (row inside a `TD` graph). mermaid 12.1.0, mermaid.live and GitHub do
  not: the subgraph follows its parent (column). zombie-mermaid never flips, so it
  matches 12.x. A 11.x-based comparison shows a difference that is not one.
- **Explicit `direction`.** Both versions keep it unless an edge crosses the subgraph
  boundary, or an ancestor's. An edge to or from the subgraph's own id (`X --> S`,
  `S --> Y`) does not cross it, so `direction LR` plus `X --> S` is a row. An edge to
  or from a member (`X --> a`, `c --> Y`) crosses, and the subgraph follows its
  parent. zombie-mermaid counts the subgraph's own id as inside, so it draws a column
  for the id-edge cases (#1830 fixes this).

## Layout tie-breaks and placement

Since mermaid 12.0.0, mermaid.js lays out flowcharts, state, class and ER diagrams
with ELK by default (it was dagre in 11.x; see the
[12.0.0 release notes](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/releases/tag/mermaid%4012.0.0)),
and mermaid.live renders that layout. Both engines are now ELK, but with different
options: mermaid sets no `considerModelOrder` and breaks cycles depth-first, while
zombie-mermaid uses `considerModelOrder.strategy: NODES_AND_EDGES` (set in
`packages/svg-renderer/src/layout-engine/to-elk.ts`), so node order within a layer, and
cross-axis offsets between layers, can still differ even when both assign the same
layers. The 12.1.0 comparison is in
[#1834](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/1834).

- **Sibling subgraph order and feedback edges.** zombie-mermaid still imitates
  mermaid 11's dagre layout in one place: depth-first back edges are reversed before
  ELK runs, which mermaid 12 does not do. Sibling subgraphs tied by an edge now keep
  declaration order ([#1982](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/1982)), so
  "Nested Subgraphs" is 100% horizontal. The remaining difference is in "CI/CD Pipeline",
  where mermaid 12.1.0 keeps `Fix & Retry` beside `Build Image` and ours puts it below
  `QA Approved?` (horizontal 90% before the dead-band below, 100% after). Tracked in
  [#1904](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/1904).
- **Remaining small differences are tie-breaks.** "System Architecture" scores 89%
  vertical against 12.2.0 (node-size tie-break, #2058) and is the accepted remaining
  difference; "Flowchart: CJK Labels" is 100% since #2358. Every
  disagreeing node pair is one renderer calling two centres level (within the 20 px
  tolerance) and the other offsetting them. In "LR Fan-In With Bypass Edge" `B` sits
  above `A` and `C` in both renderers, 22 px in mermaid (12.1.0 and 12.2.0) and 15 px
  in ours, whose boxes are 37 px tall to mermaid's 48 px (#2058). "CJK Labels"
  used to differ too (mermaid put `B` about 19 px below `A`, `C` and `D`, ours 29 px above):
  with the feedback edge `C --> A` reversed, its track sat on the wrong side of `B`. Listing
  subgraph feedback edges first in the ELK edge order fixes it (100% on 12.1.0, #2358; the
  issue was #1941).
  "Flowchart: Five Cluster Exit Siblings (TD)"
  agreed only after `elk.spacing.edgeEdge` was raised to 40 px for graphs with three or
  more labelled edges between the same pair (#1943).
- **The 20 px tolerance has a dead-band.** A fixed cut-off split pairs whose offsets
  sat on either side of it ("LR Bypass Edge In A Chain": 15 px in ours, 22 px in
  mermaid, from 37 px against 48 px boxes). A pair now also agrees when both layouts'
  offsets are within 10 px of the tolerance and point the same way (`TOLERANCE_BAND`).
  Measured on mermaid 12.1.0 across all 105 samples: 29 of 1802 pair-axes disagreed,
  13 of them such splits; the band clears 15 and moves no sample under its floor. The
  bypass, "Dense Duplicate Edges (LR)", "Self-Loop ... (LR)" and "CI/CD Pipeline"
  samples now score 100%. "Dense Duplicate Edges (TD)" (`c` 18.5 px right of `a`, 30.1 px in
  mermaid, 0.1 px outside the band) and "Self-Loop ... (TD)" (mermaid staggers 48 and 37 px, ours stacks) stay
  under the default floor, as do and "State: Notes".
  A fixed 15, 25 or 30 px tolerance, or one scaled by node height, only moved the
  cliff or split other samples; marking samples "oracle n/a" would not reach the
  non-ASCII ones (#2155).

## State diagram notes

zombie-mermaid's parser reads `note left of X` / `note right of X` but ignores the side:
swapping the keywords gives byte-identical output, and placement comes from the layout
engine's dotted edge from the state to the note ([#2094](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/2094)).
mermaid.js does not place notes on the named side either. Checked on mermaid 12.2.0
(jsDelivr, real Chrome, default config) for the "State: Notes" sample: `note right of
Active` lands below `Active`, 20 px to its left, and `note left of Idle` lands above
`Idle`, 20 px to its right. The maintainer-run oracle on 12.1.0 gives the same layout.
The remaining gap is layout tie-breaks, which is why "State: Notes" scores 83% horizontal
agreement; the floor in `scripts/lib/layout-agreement.ts` stays at 0.8
([#1942](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/1942)). Not checked: mermaid.live
or GitHub for this sample.

## Escaped characters in pie titles

mermaid.js double-escapes `<`, `&` and `>` in a pie title: `pie title Labels <&> "quotes"`
renders the text `Labels &lt;&amp;&gt; "quotes"` (the entities appear literally; the
quotes are fine). Checked on mermaid 12.2.0 (jsDelivr, real Chrome) and on mermaid.live
(version not shown on the page), by reading the rendered title element's text. zombie-mermaid
renders the literal `Labels <&> "quotes"` and does not copy the bug. Duplicate slice
labels such as `"R&D"` keep the first value in both renderers
([#2084](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/2084)).

## Pie charts

Found in the #1592 snapshot audit and re-checked on mermaid 12.2.0 (the pin, which is
also the latest on npm) for #2314; the audit also checked 12.1.0, what GitHub renders.

- **Palette.** zombie-mermaid colours slices with a blue/teal scale derived from the
  theme accent; mermaid uses its pastel `pie1`..`pie12` scale (`#ECECFF`, `#ffffde`, ...).
  `themeVariables` `pie1`..`pie12` are honoured only when opted in (see the
  `themeVariables` section below).
- **Empty pie.** When every slice is zero, zombie-mermaid draws a full outline circle;
  mermaid draws a half arc, which reads as a rendering glitch.
- **ASCII legend.** Mermaid has no ASCII output. The table lists every slice with its
  share of the whole total, including slices that get no bar cell (under 1%, or past the
  bar's 50-cell budget); a nonzero share that rounds to 0% reads `<1%`
  ([#2313](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/2313)).

## Quadrant charts

Checked on mermaid 12.2.0 (the pin, also npm `latest`). `pnpm run quadrant:oracle`
renders every `Quadrant:` sample through real mermaid and compares rect, line, circle and
text positions with `layoutQuadrantChart`; they match exactly, and the weekly layout-oracle
workflow fails on a drift (`packages/svg-renderer/src/__tests__/quadrant-svg.test.ts` also
pins the campaigns numbers). Colours and empty labels (below) are not compared.

- **Point colour.** Mermaid 12.2.0's default theme emits `fill="hsl(240, 100%, NaN%)"`
  for every point without a `color`, which browsers drop, so mermaid.live and GitHub show
  near-black dots. zombie-mermaid draws them in `var(--fg)`: the same dot on a light
  theme, still visible on a dark one. A point's own `color`, `stroke-color` and
  `stroke-width` (or its class's) are drawn as written.
- **Palette.** Cell fills are the theme accent mixed into the background at four falling
  strengths; mermaid uses lavender steps from its `primaryColor`.
- **Text widths.** Neither renderer measures text; this library's font is not mermaid's
  `trebuchet ms`, so a long label overflows at a slightly different point.
- **Not read yet.** `quadrantChart` config in `%%{init}%%` (`chartWidth`, `pointRadius`,
  `xAxisPosition`, ...) and the `quadrant*Fill` / `quadrantPoint*` theme variables are
  ignored; the chart is always 500 x 500.
- **Empty labels.** Mermaid draws an empty `<text>` for a quadrant with no label; this
  library draws nothing.
- **ASCII.** Mermaid has no ASCII output. The x axis is always below the grid (mermaid's
  SVG puts it on top of a chart with no points), and point labels are in a legend, not
  next to the markers.

## XY charts

Found in the #1592 snapshot audit and re-checked on mermaid 12.2.0 for #2314 (the audit
also covered 12.1.0). Unless noted, these are choices, not bugs.

- **SVG styling.** zombie-mermaid draws rounded bars, a dotted grid, point markers on
  lines, monotone-smoothed lines on vertical charts (horizontal charts use straight
  segments in category order, as mermaid does, [#2334](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/2334)), a generated `Bar 1` / `Line 1` legend when there is more
  than one series, and grouped bar series side by side. Mermaid draws square bars, no grid,
  no markers, no legend and straight line segments, and draws the second bar series over
  the first.
- **Horizontal charts.** The value axis sits at the bottom; mermaid puts it at the top
  (its `top-axis` group).
- **Unquoted labels keep their spaces.** `x-axis [New Users, Returning]` shows `New Users`;
  mermaid 12.2.0 renders `NewUsers`.
- **Degenerate ranges.** An all-zero series gets a -0.1..0.1 axis and a single value 42
  gets 41.9..42.1, so the data has a visible scale; mermaid shows one lone `0` or `42`
  tick and no scale.
- **ASCII y-axis.** Mermaid has no ASCII output. The plot is 20 rows tall, fewer than
  mermaid's ~10 d3 ticks need once they round to rows, so the renderer labels every Nth
  tick (the smallest N that leaves an unlabeled row between labels) rather than putting
  labels on adjacent rows
  ([#2310](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/2310)).

## ASCII: LR/RL sibling gap is `paddingY - 1` ([#2350](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/2350))

Intentional. In LR (and RL) layouts the blank-row gap between sibling nodes is `paddingY - 1` (never below 1),
4 rows at the default of 5, against mermaid 12.2.0's 40 px gap between 48 px nodes. TD keeps
`paddingY` as is. Because of the offset, `-y 5` no longer gives the old LR gap; pass `-y 6`
for it.

## ASCII: several sources into one target share the target's face

Intentional ([#1826](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/1826)). The ASCII
renderer gives each of several edges between the _same pair_ of nodes its own lane and
arrowhead (`assignParallelEdgeLanes`, `packages/ascii-renderer/src/edge-routing.ts`), and
lengthens the box face when there are more than three. Edges from _different sources_ into
one target are left out of that: they keep merging onto the target's face. Giving each
its own face cell would change `Labeled Fan-In (LR)` and widen every fan-in diagram. No
output target (charset, width, markdown profile, MCP) forces this; it is a choice.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A -->|one| T
  B -->|two| T
  C -->|three| T
  D -->|four| T
```

- **zombie-mermaid (ASCII).** The four edges join into one trunk ending in a single
  arrowhead on `T` (`TD` does the same, one head per side). Each label stays on its own
  source's stroke, so every edge is still readable and attributable, but a reader cannot
  count four heads.
- **mermaid.js.** Four separate paths, each with its own arrowhead, stacked against the
  same face of `T`. The heads overlap and the stack looks cramped, but there are four.

Checked on mermaid 12.1.0 (the pinned `node_modules` build, rendered headless in Playwright
Chromium through `scripts/lib/real-mermaid.ts`; four `flowchart-link` paths, four
`marker-end` arrowheads, both `LR` and `TD`) and on the current renderer's ASCII output
(unicode charset). Not checked: mermaid 11.x, mermaid 12.2.0 or later, mermaid.live and
GitHub for this sample, the `ascii` charset, and fan-ins with more than the four sources
above.

## ASCII: a self-loop sits on the flow-side faces, not where mermaid puts it

Not fixed ([#2101](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/2101)). Mermaid
12.1.0 and 12.2.0 (and mermaid.live, which runs 12.2.0) draw `a --> a` as a small loop on
the node's **left** face in `TD` and `BT`, and on its **top** face in `LR` and `RL`,
alone or beside other edges. The ASCII renderer draws it on the flow-side faces: out of
the bottom and back in at the right in `TD`/`BT`, out of the right and back in at the
bottom in `LR`/`RL` (`selfReferenceDirection`, `edge-routing.ts`).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  a --> a
  b --> a
  a --> c
  b --> c
  c --> a
```

- **Why not moved.** The left (`TD`/`BT`) or top (`LR`/`RL`) face of a node in the first
  grid column or row has no gutter beside it, so the layout would have to grow a leading
  column or row for it, and in the middle of a diagram that face is usually another
  edge's. The loop's legs, its arrowhead cell, duplicate loops, hugging a neighbour's lane
  (`hugLoop`, #2025/#2070) and labelled loops are all built around the current faces, so
  the move touches every self-loop, for a difference in where a small loop is drawn.
- **What does hold.** The loop shares no stroke with another edge ([#2098](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/2098)),
  and the edges around it get a stroke and an arrowhead each ([#2100](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/2100)).
- **Layout.** The two samples sit under the default 85% oracle floor for a placement
  reason that has nothing to do with the loop: mermaid staggers the three nodes
  (`SAMPLE_FLOORS`, `scripts/lib/layout-agreement.ts`).

Checked on mermaid 12.1.0 and 12.2.0 (headless Playwright) and mermaid.live (12.2.0, `TD`
only); GitHub's render was not reachable. See the comment on #2101 for the numbers.

## ASCII: node shapes are character-cell silhouettes ([#2164](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/2164))

The owner decided nodes may grow (width or rows) to get a mermaid silhouette, one shape
family per PR. Done: **stadium**, **hexagon**, **diamond**, **circle**, **subroutine**, **asymmetric** and **trapezoid**. Mermaid 12.2.0 (the pin and npm latest
agree) draws a stadium as a pill with semicircular ends and a hexagon with points at the
left and right middle.

- **Stadium.** Rounded top and bottom rows (`╭─╮` / `╰─╯`, `.-.` / `'-'` in ASCII) with `(` `)` on
  every row between. Same grid cell as before. A character grid cannot draw a true
  semicircle, so the ends are the `(` `)` glyphs, not a curve.
- **Hexagon.** Diagonals `╱ ╲` (`/ \`) cost one column per row and meet at `<` `>` on the
  middle row. A one-line label keeps the rectangle's width; a taller label, or a narrow one
  next to a tall one, grows the node so the diagonal stays a cell clear of the text.
  When a neighbour makes the row count even there are two point rows.
- **Charsets and wide glyphs.** No fallback to the old corner glyphs was needed: every
  border glyph is one cell wide in both charsets, so a CJK or emoji label (two cells per
  glyph) never moves the border, and `/ \ < >` read as a hexagon in ASCII.
- **Edges.** They still attach at the box faces (middle row on the sides, middle column on
  top and bottom); a side edge starts beside the `(`/`)`/`<`/`>` point instead of replacing it.
- **Diamond** (`{x}`). A rhombus with `<` `>` at the left and right middle and the top and
  bottom rows as a point (`╱╲` / `╲╱`, `/\` / `\/` in ASCII). The node keeps its row count
  (5 at the default padding), so the slope is whatever lands the points on the centre:
  two columns per row for a short label, shallower and sparser for a wide one. Mermaid's
  diamond is as tall as it is wide, which a terminal cannot afford, so a wide-label diamond
  is flatter than mermaid's. Widths are rounded up to an even count so the top point is two
  glyphs; when a neighbour makes the width odd the point has a `─` between them. An edge
  leaving the top or bottom starts beside the point glyph rather than replacing it.
- **Circle** (`((x))`). An ellipse: rounded top and bottom rows, `╱ ╲` on the rows between,
  `(` `)` on the middle row (`.-.` / `'-'`, `/ \` in ASCII). Mermaid's circle is round in
  pixels; the cell grid makes it about twice as wide as tall, so it is a 7-column,
  5-row minimum shape, not a true circle. Edges attach as for the stadium.
- **Corner glyphs of the outline.** `╭ ╮ ╰ ╯ . '` and the diagonals are now protected from
  an edge stroke like `( ) < >` are, so a port on a corner column starts beside it.
- **Subroutine** (`[[x]]`). Mermaid 12.2.0 draws a rectangle with a second vertical line
  just inside each side. Ours is the same: `┌┬──┬┐` / `││ x ││` / `└┴──┴┘` (`+` and `|` in
  ASCII), two columns wider than a plain box. The inner bars are on the node's own columns,
  so edges still attach at the outer border and the invariants are unchanged.
- **Asymmetric** (`>x]`, partial match). Mermaid 12.2.0 (also the npm latest) draws a
  rectangle with an inward point on the left side, in every direction (RL does not mirror
  it). Ours is a plain box whose left wall is blank on the middle row with a `>` tip one
  cell in and `╲` / `╱` on the rows beside it (`\` / `/` in ASCII; they replace the left
  corners in a 3-row box), widened by a column so the label clears the tip.
  Edges still attach at the outer border, so an edge arriving on the notch stops one cell
  short of the tip (`►` then a blank, then `>`); an edge leaving from the notch face in RL
  starts at the tip's neighbour (`┤>`). Mermaid's diagonal sides are not drawn.
- **Trapezoid** (`[/x\]`, `[\x/]`). Mermaid 12.2.0 (also the npm latest) slants both sides
  by half the node's height over its height, wide edge at the bottom for `[/x\]` and at
  the top for `[\x/]`, in every direction (BT does not flip it). Ours slants one column
  per row (`╱ ╲` / `/ \`; a cell is about half as wide as tall, so the slope matches),
  and the base row is `╱──╲` like the narrow one, so a node is wider by its slant (at
  least `2 × rows + 1` columns). A label row that would touch the slant flattens it
  there. Side edges attach at the node's outer face, then a post-pass extends the stroke
  (and moves an arrowhead) across the blank cells to the slanted wall.
- **Still approximated** (later PRs, per the owner's one-family-per-PR call): double circle
  (needs a second, concentric ellipse: a width and height decision) and parallelograms
  (slanted sides cost one column per row, so a node widens by its slant, and the RL
  mirroring from #1701 must keep the lean).

## ASCII: LR skip edge beside a reciprocal pair (partial match)

[#2100](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/2100). For the `LR`/`RL` form
of the sample above, the renderer now follows mermaid 12.2.0's topology: `b --> a` and
`b --> c` leave `b` on separate rows, `b --> c` runs under `a` with an arrowhead of its
own at `c`, the loop on `a` sits above it, and `a --> c` / `c --> a` are two strokes
between `a` and `c`. It is not a full match:

- **`b --> c` enters `c`'s bottom face.** Mermaid enters `c`'s left face. A second
  stroke on the left face would need a taller box.
- **The loop leaves `a`'s right face and re-enters its top.** Mermaid leaves and
  re-enters the top. The first row gets a blank margin row for it.
- **Narrow trigger** (`backStraight`, `edge-routing.ts`): `LR`/`RL`, no subgraphs, no
  labels on the pair, a skip edge sharing an end with the pair, no loop on that skip
  edge's ends, and at most 3 non-loop edges in total on each node of the pair (the
  pair's own two edges plus one more, the skip edge). Busier shapes and every other
  reciprocal pair keep the U under the row.
- **Boxes on the pair take 5 rows.** The two strokes need three cells on each side
  face (a 3-row box has one), so the pair's nodes grow, as boxes with several side-face
  edges already do. Mermaid's boxes do not change height.

Checked against mermaid 12.2.0 (the pin and npm latest), headless via
`scripts/lib/real-mermaid.ts`.

## Class: lollipop interfaces

Not a difference any more for one-ended lollipops
([#2117](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/2117),
[#2135](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/2135)): `A ()-- B` / `B --() A` draw
the name beside a small circle joined to `B` by a stem, with no `A` box unless `A` has
members, an annotation, another relationship, a note or a namespace, in both SVG and ASCII,
as mermaid.js does (12.1.0 and 12.2.0 agree). `()--()` is an ordinary boxed line with a
circle at both ends, in mermaid and here.

Dotted lollipops (`()..`, `..()`), which mermaid accepts, are a parse error here.

## Class: edge corners in SVG

mermaid 12.1.0 and 12.2.0 draw class edges orthogonally with 7 px rounded corners (not
smooth curves, [#2104](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/2104)); ours has
sharp corners. Relationship labels sit on the edge over a background plate in both.

## Class: LR and RL in ASCII

Class diagrams with `direction LR` or `direction RL` are drawn in ASCII like the SVG, with
each level in a column and `RL` as the mirror
([#2158](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/2158); mermaid.js 12.1.0 and 12.2.0
agree on the arrangement). The top-down and `BT` drawings are the class renderer's own level
rows; `LR` and `RL` are lowered onto the flowchart ASCII grid instead (classes become boxed
nodes, relationships become edges, namespaces become frames), so a few things follow the
flowchart, not mermaid:

- Boxes in a column share one width and boxes on a row share one height; the extra rows stay
  empty at the bottom of the last compartment (a box with one compartment is centred).
  mermaid.js keeps each box at its own size.
- A parent with several children leaves by one face and branches off a shared trunk, instead
  of one line per child from the parent's flow-side face.
- A line that meets a box side on a compartment divider row is joined to it (`┼`); it can
  look as if it crosses the box.
- Namespace frames, labels and routing around obstacles are the flowchart's, so they differ
  in detail from the top-down class drawing.

`RenderOptions.direction` still does not apply to class diagrams.

## `themeVariables` are opt-in, and only a subset

Decided in [#2108](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/2108).
Mermaid applies `%%{init: {"themeVariables": {...}}}%%`; zombie-mermaid ignores it
unless the caller sets `honorThemeVariables: true`, because the colours of a
diagram should come from the host's `bg`/`fg` theme, not from text inside the
diagram. Checked on mermaid 12.1.0 and 12.2.0 (headless Chromium, computed
paint, identical results):

| Input                                                                                             | mermaid.js 12.1.0 / 12.2.0              | zombie-mermaid                                   |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `theme: base` + `primaryColor`, flowchart                                                         | node fill follows it                    | ignored; with the option: node fill (`surface`)  |
| `primaryColor` under the default, `dark`, `forest`, `neutral` themes                              | ignored                                 | same                                             |
| `primaryTextColor`, `primaryBorderColor` (`base`)                                                 | text colour; start of a border gradient | ignored; with the option: `fg`; a solid `border` |
| `lineColor`, any theme                                                                            | edge and arrowhead colour               | ignored; with the option: `line`                 |
| `pie1`..`pie12`, any theme                                                                        | the Nth slice in source order, wrapping | ignored; with the option: same                   |
| invalid `primaryColor` (`#12345`)                                                                 | throws `Unsupported color format`       | ignored, renders                                 |
| invalid `pie1` (`notacolor`)                                                                      | slice painted `#333`                    | ignored, theme colour kept                       |
| `secondaryColor`, `tertiaryColor`, `background`, `fontFamily`, `nodeBorder`, `pie*TextColor`, ... | applied or used to derive other colours | not supported, listed in `InitConfig.ignored`    |

Mermaid derives many colours from `primaryColor` (secondary/tertiary, subgraph
fill, the border gradient, the other pie slices); zombie-mermaid does not, so a
`base` diagram with only `primaryColor` set does not look the same in both. Only
flowchart, state and pie read the directive. Details and the opt-in table:
[Configuration directives](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/blob/main/docs/diagrams.md#themevariables-opt-in).

## Invalid colours are ignored, not refused

Decided in [#2345](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/2345) (policy from
[#1523](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/1523)). An invalid colour in a
`style`/`classDef` line (`fill:notacolor`, `stroke:#zzz`) does not fail the render:
mermaid.js 12.1.0 and 12.2.0 render the diagram without raising, and the browser drops
the bad declaration, so the default paint stays. zombie-mermaid also renders and drops
the value (it never reaches the SVG). The agentic-mermaid project refuses such input by
name instead. The difference is deliberate, not a gap: parity with mermaid.js here means
tolerating the input. (An invalid `themeVariables` colour is a separate case, listed in
the table above, where mermaid itself throws.)

## ASCII: opt-in layout-faithful mode (`--layout mermaid`)

The default ASCII renderer lays flowcharts out on its own grid, so node order and spacing
differ from mermaid's. `zombie-mermaid render <file> --ascii --layout mermaid` (library:
`renderMermaidASCIIWithLayout(src, { layout: 'mermaid' })` from `zombie-mermaid/ascii-layout`)
instead draws mermaid's own ELK layout (`packages/elk-layout`, `packages/ascii-layout`; #2177).
Opt-in only: without the flag the output is byte-identical to before.

- **Fallback, never silent.** Subgraphs, shapes the layout does not model, non-flowchart
  diagrams, a layout error, or a missing `elkjs-0.9.3` make it use the standard renderer; the
  CLI prints `layout-faithful: <reason>; used standard renderer` on stderr and the API returns
  `path: 'standard'` plus `fallbackReason`. On success stderr says `layout-faithful: used
  mermaid's ELK layout` and the result carries a `note`.
- **Width cap and fallback.** The drawing is capped at 120 columns (`--max-width <n>` /
  `maxCols` sets another cap): blank gaps between node groups are shrunk to fit, boxes never
  are. A diagram whose boxes alone exceed the cap (e.g. a long LR chain of wide labels) falls
  back to the standard renderer by default, with `layout-faithful: layout-faithful output is N
  columns, over the 120-column cap; used standard renderer` on stderr (API: `fallbackReason`).
  To get the wide layout-faithful text anyway, use `--layout mermaid-wide` (API:
  `maxCols: Infinity`).
- **Merged lines hide edge multiplicity.** Identical parallel edges draw as one line (three
  `A --> B` look like one).
- **Plain drawing at a fixed scale.** `-x/-y/-p`, `--coords`, `--theme` colors, `--hyperlinks`
  and `--max-width` compaction (it is the column cap instead) do not apply to it (they apply to a fallback render).
- **Pinned to mermaid 12.1.0 + elkjs 0.9.3.** The layout is only faithful to that pair. The
  repo's oracle pin is now 12.2.0, and `pnpm run elk-layout:oracle` on 12.2.0 differs from
  12.1.0 in three gallery samples (circle and double-circle node sizes in "Original Node
  Shapes" and "Subroutine and Hexagon Shapes", one edge path in "Labeled Fan-In (LR)"); the module still
  matches 12.1.0, which is what GitHub renders. The module is not yet updated to 12.2.0.
- **Dependency.** `elkjs-0.9.3` (`npm:elkjs@0.9.3`) is an optional peer dependency of
  `zombie-mermaid`, kept separate from the `elkjs` 0.11/0.12 the SVG renderer uses. The layout
  code is bundled into lazy chunks that load only when the option is used. The MCP tool does not
  expose it.

## C4: a title-only diagram draws its title

`C4Context` with a `title` and no elements: mermaid.js 12.1.0 and 12.2.0 both emit
`viewBox="0 -70 200 187"` with the title at `x="-150"`, which is left of the
viewBox, so the title is clipped and invisible (checked headless in Chromium, #2282).
zombie-mermaid deliberately draws it: the SVG canvas is `2 * 50 + title width` by 80,
with the title inside, and the ASCII output prints the title (mermaid has no ASCII
output). A diagram with no title, elements, or boundaries still renders nothing.

## Known limitations (not intentional, not yet fixed)

## ER diagrams

zombie-mermaid's ER parser (`packages/mermaid-parser/src/er/parser.ts`) is a
line-oriented parser rather than mermaid.js's grammar, so it is more lenient in
some places and stricter in others.

**Unquoted labels that start with a keyword.** Everything after `:` is the label here.
mermaid.js lexes a leading `one`, `many` or `to` as a word-form cardinality keyword
and rejects the line:

| Label                                                        | mermaid.js 11.17.2 | zombie-mermaid |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------ | -------------- |
| `one-to-one`, `many-to-many`, `one`, `many`, `to` (unquoted) | parse error        | renders        |
| `"one-to-one"`, `"many-to-many"` (quoted)                    | parses             | renders        |
| `opt-to-many` (unquoted)                                     | parses             | renders        |

Quote such labels (`: "one-to-one"`) if the source also has to work in mermaid.js
tools such as GitHub or the Mermaid Live Editor.

---

# https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/blob/main/docs/react-integration.md

# React Integration

Because rendering is synchronous, you can call `renderMermaidSVG()` directly in the render body — no `useEffect` round trip, no flash. Wrapping the call in `useMemo()` additionally skips recomputing the SVG on renders where `code` hasn't changed:

```tsx
import ELK from 'elkjs/lib/elk.bundled.js'
import { registerElk, renderMermaidSVG } from 'zombie-mermaid'

registerElk(ELK) // once, at app startup, before the first render

function MermaidDiagram({ code }: { code: string }) {
  const { svg, error } = React.useMemo(() => {
    try {
      return {
        svg: renderMermaidSVG(code, {
          bg: 'var(--background)',
          fg: 'var(--foreground)',
          transparent: true,
        }),
        error: null,
      }
    } catch (err) {
      return {
        svg: null,
        error: err instanceof Error ? err : new Error(String(err)),
      }
    }
  }, [code])

  if (error) return <pre>{error.message}</pre>
  return <div dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: svg! }} />
}
```

**Setup:** in a browser, flowchart, state, class, ER and architecture diagrams throw `ElkNotRegisteredError` until you call `registerElk()`, so run `npm install elkjs` and register it as above. Sequence, pie, xychart and C4 diagrams need nothing. To keep `elkjs` out of your initial bundle, register it lazily instead: `const { default: ELK } = await import('elkjs/lib/elk.bundled.js'); registerElk(ELK)`, and render only after that resolves. See [guides/elkjs-optional-peer.md](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/blob/main/docs/guides/elkjs-optional-peer.md).

**Why this works well:**

- **No flash** — SVG is computed synchronously during render, not in a useEffect (once `elkjs` is registered)
- **CSS variables** — Pass `var(--background)` etc. instead of hex colors. The SVG inherits from your app's CSS, so theme switches apply instantly without re-rendering
- **Memoized** — Only recomputed when `code` changes
- **Links and hover stay interactive** — `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` inlines the SVG into your page's DOM. An `<img src="data:image/svg+xml,...">` approach would render the SVG in the browser's secure static mode instead, where `click`-generated links and CSS `:hover` tooltips go inert — see [`docs/decisions/no-script-interactivity.md`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/blob/main/docs/decisions/no-script-interactivity.md) for why

**With the React Compiler:** the manual `useMemo()` above is the pattern for codebases without the compiler enabled. If your project has the [React Compiler](https://react.dev/learn/react-compiler) turned on, it memoizes this call automatically — you can call `renderMermaidSVG()` directly in the component body and drop the `useMemo()` wrapper. The synchronous, no-`useEffect` part still matters either way; only the manual memoization becomes redundant.

## Strict Content-Security-Policy

If your app ships a `style-src` without `'unsafe-inline'`, the diagram's two inline-style surfaces — the `<style>` element and the root `<svg style="--bg: …">` attribute carrying the theme variables — are both blocked, and it renders unstyled ([issue #216](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/216)). A nonce can allow the element but never the attribute, so use both options together and move the variables into a nonced stylesheet you control:

```tsx
import { renderMermaidSVG, themeCssVariables } from 'zombie-mermaid'

function MermaidDiagram({ code, nonce }: { code: string; nonce: string }) {
  const opts = {
    bg: 'var(--background)',
    fg: 'var(--foreground)',
    transparent: true,
    nonce, // every <style> in the SVG gets nonce="…"
    styleAttribute: false, // no root style= attribute
  }
  const svg = React.useMemo(() => renderMermaidSVG(code, opts), [code, nonce])
  const css = `.mermaid svg { ${themeCssVariables(opts)} }`
  return (
    <>
      <style nonce={nonce}>{css}</style>
      <div className="mermaid" dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: svg }} />
    </>
  )
}
```

`themeCssVariables()` returns the exact declarations the attribute would have carried, so pass it the same options. If the theme colours are static you can put that rule in your regular external stylesheet instead of a nonced `<style>`; `styleAttribute: false` is the only part that must be set at render time.

---

# https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/blob/main/docs/migrating-from-beautiful-mermaid.md

# Migrating from `beautiful-mermaid`

`zombie-mermaid` is a maintained fork of [`beautiful-mermaid`](https://github.com/lukilabs/beautiful-mermaid) — see the [README](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/blob/main/README.md#why-this-fork-exists) for why the fork exists. The core render functions keep the same signatures, but since 3.0 this is not a pure package-name swap: see [Breaking changes since the fork](#breaking-changes-since-the-fork).

But "drop-in" is about the API, not the pixels. Part of what this fork does is fix Mermaid syntax that `beautiful-mermaid` parsed incorrectly or silently mishandled. If you already have diagrams in production — stored source rendered on the fly, or SVGs generated once and cached — some of them may render differently the moment you upgrade. Nothing here is a bug in the new behavior; each fix below makes the output match what Mermaid itself, and the diagram author, actually intended. But a silent visual change is still worth knowing about before it shows up in a support ticket.

This page covers what's safe to assume unchanged, itemizes the fixes most likely to change existing rendered output, and gives you a cheap way to check your own diagrams before upgrading.

## Breaking changes since the fork

- **Node `>=24`** is required (`engines.node` in `package.json`).
- **`registerElk()`**: in browsers and bundlers, flowchart, state, class, ER and architecture diagrams throw `ElkNotRegisteredError` until you `npm install elkjs` and call `registerElk(ELK)` once. Node, Bun, the CLI and MCP load it automatically. See [guides/elkjs-optional-peer.md](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/blob/main/docs/guides/elkjs-optional-peer.md).
- **Packages**: the parser and renderers live under `packages/*` (there is no `src/` library layout to deep-import from).

A full 2.x to 5.x upgrade guide is tracked in [#1538](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/1538).

## What is drop-in

- `renderMermaidSVG`, `renderMermaidSVGAsync`, `renderMermaidASCII`, and `parseMermaid` all have the same signatures as in `beautiful-mermaid`.
- `registerElk` is new: required in browsers, see above. `renderMermaidSVG` (synchronous) is this fork's primary SVG entry point, and C4, architecture, pie and xychart diagrams and the MCP server are new here, with no `beautiful-mermaid` behavior to match.
- `RenderOptions` and `AsciiRenderOptions` — colors, fonts, spacing, theming — work the same way. See [api-reference.md](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/blob/main/docs/api-reference.md).
- `mergeEdges` is new to this fork's `RenderOptions` — `beautiful-mermaid` has no equivalent option, so there's no prior behavior it needs to match.
- Built-in themes, Shiki compatibility, and CSS-variable-driven live theme switching are unchanged.
- The CLI (`zombie-mermaid` binary) is new to this fork — `beautiful-mermaid` never had one — so there's no prior behavior it needs to preserve.

If your code only calls these functions with diagram source and a `RenderOptions` object, no code changes are required beyond the import/package name, plus `registerElk()` in browsers and Node `>=24`.

## Output-affecting fixes

Each of these changes what gets drawn for Mermaid syntax that previously parsed into something else — not new syntax support for things `beautiful-mermaid` simply didn't have. If none of the trigger syntax below appears in your stored diagrams, none of this applies to you; the audit recipe in the next section tells you for certain either way.

### `classDef` / `class` styling

This is the fix most likely to affect a real diagram, because `classDef`/`class` is common Mermaid syntax and `beautiful-mermaid`'s support for it had several sharp edges. Most of these shipped together in this fork's [v1.2.0](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/releases/tag/v1.2.0) release; the last one (`classDef default`) needs [v1.3.0](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/releases/tag/v1.3.0):

- **A trailing semicolon on a `class` statement produced a stray node.** `class B highlight;` — completely valid, optional Mermaid syntax — fell through class-assignment parsing (which required unterminated `\w+$`) into node parsing, so instead of styling node `B` the diagram grew an extra node literally labeled `class`. Fixed in [#53](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/53).
- **`:::className` before the shape brackets dropped the node's label entirely.** `A:::external[External User]` matched none of the shape-detection regexes (they require the id immediately before its brackets), so it fell back to a bare-id match and `[External User]` was discarded. Fixed in [#77](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/77).
- **Custom classes never appeared as a `class` attribute on the SVG element**, even though the class's `fill`/`stroke` were already applied inline — so any external CSS meant to target `.highlight` had nothing to select. Fixed in [#75](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/75).
- **Text on a custom-fill node could render unreadable.** A node styled via `classDef`/`class`/`style` with a `fill` but no explicit `color` always fell back to the ambient theme text color — white-on-light or black-on-dark, depending on the fill and the active theme. `packages/svg-renderer/src/renderer.ts` now computes a readable black/white text color from the fill's own luminance whenever the fill resolves to a concrete color (via `getReadableTextColor` in `packages/core/src/theme.ts`), only falling back to the theme color when the fill is a CSS variable or otherwise unresolvable. Fixed in [#76](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/76).
- **`style A font-family:...` and `classDef`-supplied `font-family` were parsed but never rendered**, silently ignored in SVG output. Fixed in [#78](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/78).
- **`classDef default` only applied to nodes that named it explicitly** (`class X default`), instead of styling every node the way Mermaid does it. Fixed in [#206](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/206) (v1.3.0).

Parsing lives in `packages/mermaid-parser/src/flowchart-parser.ts` around `graph.classDefs`/`graph.classAssignments`; resolution into inline node styles is in `packages/svg-renderer/src/renderer.ts`.

**Triggered by:** any diagram using `classDef`, `class`, `:::className`, or `style` — especially one with a trailing semicolon on a `class` line, a `:::className` shorthand before the node's brackets, or a custom fill without an explicit text color.

### SVG coordinates rounded to 2 decimal places

All SVG coordinates are now rounded to 2dp, which changes every SVG output string (byte-for-byte). Rendering is visually identical; only snapshot or string-equality tests on stored SVG need regenerating.

### Brackets inside quoted labels, and no-space arrows

`A["/blog/[slug]"]` previously rendered as `"/blog/[slug` — the shape-delimiter matcher used a lazy `.+?` to find the closing `]`, so it stopped at the first `]` it found, including one inside the quoted string. Any label containing a literal `[` or `]` — file globs, route patterns, array-index notation — was silently truncated. Delimiter matching is now quote-aware, so a complete `"..."` span is treated as a unit.

The same fix ([#80](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/80), landed in v1.2.0) also fixed `A-->B` (no space around the arrow): the bare-node-id pattern greedily consumed the arrow's leading dashes, producing a bogus node `A--` and dropping the edge entirely.

**Triggered by:** a quoted node/edge label containing `[`, `]`, `(`, `)`, `{`, or `}`; or a flowchart edge written with no space before the arrow (`A-->B` rather than `A --> B`).

### Semicolons as statement separators
